items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: A fellow by the name of Jonas Walker came from St. Louis to New York and the trombone players heard him... so he was the first trombone player with Duke before Tricky Sam

ctx.x: How large was the band at that time?

Five pieces when they were at the Kentucky Club. Yes, five pieces. Then they added on a trombone player name of Charlie Irvis who did the plunger bit, the Tricky Sam, he created that. There was a fellow came from St. Louis did the wah-wah, the first one we heard do the plunger bit that Johnny Dunn had created back in 1920, and then invented the plunger. A fellow by the name of Jonas Walker came from St. Louis to New York and the trombone players heard him, so Charlie Irvis got some part of a little tin mute he…
Is that right? Was Duke, when he first came out, after Sonny Greer made the switch for him, and came out as Duke Ellington's Band, was the name of it -- overnight it was Duke Ellington's Band, right?
